body.head: A GODLY AND LEARNED EXPOSITION OF CHRISTS Sermon in the MOUNT.

epigraph.q: Care not for the morrow, for the morrow shall care for it selfe: the day hath enough with his owne griefe.

div.p: Here Christ the third time repeats his commaundement against distrustful care, propoūded first in the 25. verse.

q.p: Iudge not, that you be not iudged.
2. For with what iudgement ye iudge, yee shall be iudged; and with what measure you mete, it shall be measured to you againe.

div.p: IN these words, and so forward to the end of the fift6. part of Christs s • rmon. verse, is contained the sixt part of this sermon of our Sauiour Christ, concerning Iudgement.

epigraph.q: For with what iudgement ye iudge, ye shall be iudged: and with what measure you mete, it shall be measured to you againe.

div.p: This verse containes a double confirmation of the former reason, drawne from the euent.

q.p: And why seest thou the mote that is in thy brothers eye, and perceiuest not the beame that is in thine owne eye?
4. Or how saiest thou to thy brother, Suffer me to cast out the mote out of thine eye, and behold a beame is in thine owne eye?

div.p: These two verses containe a second reason to inforce the former cō mandement against rash iudgement.

q.p: And it came to passe when Iesus had ended these words, the people were astonied at his doctrine.
29. For he taught as one hauing authoritie, and not as the Scribes.

div.p: These two verses containe the issue and euent of this Sermon of our Sauiour Christ in his hearers.
